pages.title: FINITENESS THEOREM FOR A PROPER MORPHISM; COHOMOLOGICAL DIMENSION OF AFFINE ALGEBRAIC SCHEMES

blocks.html:
EXPOSÉ XIV
FINITENESS THEOREM FOR A PROPER MORPHISM;
COHOMOLOGICAL DIMENSION OF AFFINE ALGEBRAIC SCHEMESby M. Artin
Contents

1. Finiteness theorem for a proper morphism
2. A variant of dimension
3. Cohomological dimension of affine algebraic schemes
4. Proof of theorem 3.1
This exposé contains two important theorems which are proved using the base change theorem for a proper morphism.

pages.title: 1. Finiteness theorem for a proper morphism.

blocks.html: 1. Finiteness theorem for a proper morphism.

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 1.1

Let \(f : X \to S\) be a proper morphism of finite presentation. Let \(A\) be a left noetherian ring which is a \(\mathbb{Z}/n\)-algebra for suitable \(n \in \mathbb{N}\). Let \(F\) be a constructible sheaf of sets (resp. of groups, resp. of \(A\)-modules) on \(X\). Then the sheaf \(f_* F\) (resp. \(R^1 f_* F\), resp. \(R^q f_* F\) for each \(q \geqslant 0\)) is likewise constructible.
In particular, we have:

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 1.2

Let \(X\) be a scheme proper over the spectrum of a separably closed field \(k\), and let \(F\) be a constructible torsion abelian sheaf on \(X\). Then the groups \(H^q(X,F)\) are finite for each \(q \geqslant 0\).

blocks.title: Remark
blocks.html:
Remark 1.3

The theorem is false for abelian sheaves if one omits the condition that \(f\) be proper, as one sees by taking \(F = \mathbb{Z}/p\), \(p = \operatorname{car} k\), \(X = \mathbb{E}^1_k\), the affine space, and \(f\) the inclusion of \(X\) in \(\mathbb{P}^1_k\), or the structural morphism \(X \to \operatorname{Spec} k\). However, one conjectures that it is true if \(F\) is prime to the residue characteristics of \(S\) and \(S\) is "excellent" (EGA IV 7.8). One can prove it, when one has available the theorem of resolution of singularities (for example in characteristic zero), for an excellent scheme \(S\) of equal characteristics (XIX 5.1).

Proof of 1.1. The assertion is local on \(S\), and one may therefore take \(S\) affine. Then \(S\) is the limit of the spectra of rings of finite type over \(\mathbb{Z}\), and the data of the theorem are such that they can be obtained, by base change \(S \to S_o\), from a proper morphism \(f_o : X_o \to S_o\) with \(S_o\) of finite type over \(\mathbb{Z}\) and a constructible sheaf \(F_o\) on \(X_o\), cf. EGA IV 8 and IX 2.7.4. Now, since the inverse image of a constructible sheaf is again constructible (IX 2.4 (iii)), we are reduced, by applying XII 5.1 to the base change morphism \(S_o \leftarrow S\), to proving the constructibility of \(f_{o*} F_o\) (resp. of \(R^q f_{o*} F_o\)), whence the

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 1.4

It suffices to verify 1.1 with \(S\) of finite type over \(\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}\).

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 1.5

The set-theoretic assertion of 1.1 is true, that is, \(f_* F\) is a constructible sheaf of sets if \(F\) is.

Proof. We may assume \(S\) noetherian (1.4). Let \(F \hookrightarrow G = \prod_i \pi_{i*}(C_i)\) be an injection with \(\pi_i : X_i \to X\) finite and \(C_i\) constant and constructible on \(X_i\) (IX 2.14). We have \(f_* F \subset f_* G\), and consequently (IX 2.9 (iii)) it suffices to treat the case \(F = G\). Now \(f_* G = \prod_i (f \pi_i)_* C_i\), and a finite product of constructible sheaves on \(S\) is constructible (IX 2.14). Replacing \(X\) by \(X_i\), we are reduced to the case where \(F = D_X\) is a constant constructible sheaf, with value \(D\). Now by virtue of XII 5.1 (i), the stalk \(f_*(F)_{\bar{s}}\) is isomorphic to \(D^{C(\bar{s})}\), where \(C(\bar{s}) = \pi_o(X_{\bar{s}})\), hence it is finite. By IX 2.13 (iii) it suffices to prove that the function "number of elements of the stalk of \(f_* F\)" is constructible on \(S\). Now this function is \(\operatorname{card}(D^C)\), where \(C\) is the function "number of connected components in the geometric fibre", and \(C\) is constructible (EGA IV 9.7.9), whence the result.

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 1.6

Let \(S\) be a noetherian scheme, \(f : X \to S\) proper, \(F\) a constructible sheaf of groups (resp. of \(A\)-modules) on \(X\), \(q\) an integer equal to \(0\) or \(1\) (resp. an integer \(\geqslant 0\)). Let \(S_i\) \((1 \leqslant i \leqslant n)\) be subschemes of \(S\) such that \(S = \bigcup_i S_i\), and let \(F_i\), \(f_i : X_i \to S_i\) be the "restrictions" of the data to the \(S_i\). Then if for every \(i\), \(R^q f_{i*} F_i\) is constructible, the same holds for \(R^q f_* F\).
Proof. The restriction of \(R^q f_* F\) to \(S_i\) is isomorphic to \(R^q f_{i*} F_i\) by XII 5.1, and the lemma follows from IX 2.8.
We now proceed by arguments analogous to those of XII 8:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 1.7

Let \(S\) be noetherian,

\[\xymatrix{ X \ar[dr]_{f} & & \bar{X} \ar[ll]_{\pi} \ar[dl]^{\bar{f}} \\ & S & }\]

a commutative diagram of proper morphisms, and \(j : U \to X\) an open subset such that the open subset \(\bar{U} = U \times_X \bar{X}\) maps isomorphically onto \(U\). Let \(Y = X - U\) be the reduced closed scheme, and let \(f_o : Y \to S\) and \(i : Y \to X\) be the canonical morphisms. Suppose the theorem 1.1 true for \(\bar{f}\), \(f_o\), and \(\pi\). Then it is likewise true for \(f\).
Proof. Let us first treat the case of a sheaf of \(A\)-modules \(F\) on \(X\). We have the exact sequence

and taking into account the corresponding exact cohomology sequence for the \(R^q f_*\), and IX 2.6, we see that it suffices to verify the constructibility of the \(R^q f_*\) for the outer terms (note that \(i_* i^* F\) is constructible by IX 2.4 (ii) and IX 2.15 (i), hence so is \(j_! j^* F\) (IX 2.6)). Since \(i\) is a closed immersion,
(VIII 5.6), whence the constructibility in this case by the hypothesis on \(f_o\). Moreover, denoting by \(\bar{j} : \bar{U} \to \bar{X}\) the inclusion morphism and \(\bar{F} = \pi^* F\), we have

as one verifies by first defining an arrow \(\to\), and proving that it is invertible fibre by fibre using XII 5.1 (i). At each geometric point \(\bar{y}\) of \(Y\), the restriction of \(\bar{j}_! \bar{j}^* \bar{F}\) to the fibre \(\bar{X}_{\bar{y}}\) of \(\bar{X}\) over \(X\) is zero, and consequently by XII 5.1 (iii) the stalk of \((R^q \pi_*)(\bar{j}_! \bar{j}^* \bar{F})\) at \(\bar{y}\) is zero for each \(q \geqslant 0\). Since on the other hand \(\pi\) induces an isomorphism over \(X - Y\), we have \((R^q \pi_*)(\bar{j}_! \bar{j}^* \bar{F}) = 0\) if \(q > 0\). From the Leray spectral sequence
\[E_2^{p,q} = (R^p f_*)(R^q \pi_*)(\bar{j}_! \bar{j}^* \bar{F}) \Longrightarrow R^n \bar{f}_*(\bar{j}_! \bar{j}^* \bar{F})\]
and \((*)\), we deduce the isomorphisms
\[(R^q \bar{f}_*)(\bar{j}_! \bar{j}^* \bar{F}) \simeq (R^q f_*)(j_! j^* F)\]

for \(q \geqslant 0\). Since \(\bar{j}_! \bar{j}^* \bar{F}\) is constructible (same argument as for \(j_! j^* F\)), the right-hand side is too, whence the constructibility of \((R^q f_*)(j_! j^* F)\) and therefore of \(R^q f_* F\).

Suppose now that \(F\) is a constructible sheaf of groups on \(X\). Let us replace \(\pi : \bar{X} \to X\) by \(\pi \amalg i : (\bar{X} \amalg Y) \to X\). It thus suffices to prove that if \(\pi : \bar{X} \to X\) is surjective and if 1.1 is true for \(\pi\) and for \(\bar{f}\), then it is likewise true for \(f\). Let \(\bar{F}\) first be a constructible sheaf of groups on \(\bar{X}\). Then \(\pi_* \bar{F}\) is constructible on \(X\) (1.5), and we have an injection \((R^1 f_*) \pi_* \bar{F} \hookrightarrow (R^1 \bar{f}_*)\bar{F}\). The right-hand side is constructible by hypothesis, and consequently the left-hand side is too (IX 2.9 (ii)). Now since \(\pi\) is surjective, we have an injection \(F \to \pi_* \pi^* F = G\). The sheaf \(\bar{F} = \pi^* F\) is constructible, hence \(G\) and \(R^1 f_* G\) are also constructible, as we saw above. We are thus reduced to the following lemma:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 1.8

Let \(S\) be noetherian, \(f : X \to S\) a proper morphism, and \(F \overset{u}{\hookrightarrow} G\) an injection of constructible sheaves of groups on \(X\). If \(R^1 f_* G\) is constructible, then \(R^1 f_* F\) is too.
Proof. Let \(C = G/F\), which is a constructible sheaf of homogeneous spaces under \(G\) (apply IX 2.6). Consider the exact sequence
\[f_* C \xrightarrow{\ \delta\ } R^1 f_* F \xrightarrow{\ u^1\ } R^1 f_* G \tag{\(*\)}\]

To prove that \(R^1 f_* F\) is constructible, it suffices, by noetherian induction and 1.6, to prove that if \(S \neq \emptyset\), there exists a non-empty open subset of \(S\) on which \(R^1 f_*(F)\) is constructible. We may therefore assume \(R^1 f_* G\) locally constant, and hence, since constructibility is a local notion for the étale topology, we may assume that \(S\) is irreducible and \(R^1 f_* G\) is constant (and constructible), with value \(E = \{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}\). Let \(D_i\) \((i = 1,\ldots,n)\) be the subsheaf of \(R^1 f_* F\) that is the inverse image of the section \(e_i\) under \(u^1\). Since in a topos "sums are universal", we have \(R^1 f_* F = \amalg_i D_i\), and it therefore suffices to prove that each \(D_i\) is constructible over a suitable non-empty \(S'\) étale over \(S\).

Let us recall that \(R^1 f_* F\) is the sheaf associated with the presheaf \(\hat{R}^1 F\), where \(\hat{R}^1 F(S') = H^1(X',F)\). Consequently, we may assume (by replacing \(S\) by a non-empty \(S'\) étale over \(S\)) that \(D_i\) is the "empty" sheaf (hence constructible), or that there exists an element \(\alpha \in H^1(X,F)\) which induces a section \(\alpha\) of \(D_i\). In this latter case, let
\[f_* C^\alpha \xrightarrow{\ \delta\ } R^1 f_* F^\alpha \longrightarrow R^1 f_* G^\alpha\]
be the exact sequence deduced from \((*)\) "by twisting by means of \(\alpha\)". We have
\[R^1 f_* F^\alpha \simeq R^1 f_* F \;, \qquad R^1 f_* G^\alpha \simeq R^1 f_* G \;,\]

and the section of \(R^1 f_* F^\alpha\) corresponding to \(\bar{\alpha}\) is the unit section. Hence the subsheaf \(D_i^\alpha\) of \(R^1 f_* F^\alpha\) corresponding to \(D_i\) is the inverse image of the unit section of \(R^1 f_* G^\alpha\), i.e., \(D_i^\alpha\) is the image of \(f_* C^\alpha\) under \(\delta\). Since \(f_* C\) is constructible (1.5), the same holds for \(D_i^\alpha\), hence for \(D_i\) (apply IX 2.6), whence the lemma.

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 1.9

Let \(S\) be noetherian and

\[\xymatrix{ X \ar[dr]_{f} & & \bar{X} \ar[ll]_{\pi} \ar[dl]^{\bar{f}} \\ & S & }\]

a commutative diagram of proper morphisms. If the theorem 1.1 is true for \(f\) and \(\pi\), then it is likewise true for \(\bar{f}\).
Proof. In the case of a constructible sheaf \(\bar{F}\) of \(A\)-modules, one uses the Leray spectral sequence
\[E_2^{p,q} = (R^p f_*)(R^q \pi_*)\bar{F} \Longrightarrow (R^n \bar{f}_*)\bar{F} \;.\]
By hypothesis, one finds that \(E_2^{p,q}\) is constructible for each \(p,q\), and consequently the abutment is too, as then follows from IX 2.6.
Let \(\bar{F}\) be a constructible sheaf of groups. We have the exact sequence (XII 3.2)

where the outer terms are constructible by hypothesis and 1.5. One proceeds as in the proof of 1.8: It suffices, by noetherian induction and 1.6, to assume \(S \neq \emptyset\) and to prove constructibility over a suitable non-empty open subset. We may therefore assume \(f_*(R^1 \pi_*)\bar{F}\) locally constant, and (by étale localization) even constant and constructible (IX 2.8), with value \(E = \{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}\). Let \(D_i\) be the subsheaf of \((R^1 \bar{f}_*)\bar{F}\) that is the inverse image of \(e_i\), so that \((R^1 \bar{f}_*)\bar{F} = \amalg_i D_i\). It suffices to prove that each of the sheaves \(D_i\) induces a constructible sheaf over a suitable connected non-empty \(S'/S\) étale. If \(D_i\) is not the "empty sheaf", we reduce to the case where there exists an element \(\alpha \in H^1(\bar{X},\bar{F})\) which induces a section \(\bar{\alpha}\) of \(D_i\). Let
\[0 \to (R^1 f_*) \pi_* \bar{F}^\alpha \to (R^1 \bar{f}_*)\bar{F}^\alpha \to f_*(R^1 \pi_*)\bar{F}^\alpha\]

be the exact sequence deduced from \((*)\) by twisting \(\bar{F}\) by means of \(\alpha\). The section of \((R^1 \bar{f}_*)\bar{F}^\alpha\) corresponding to \(\bar{\alpha}\) is the unit section, and consequently the subsheaf \(D_i^\alpha\) of \((R^1 \bar{f}_*)\bar{F}^\alpha\) corresponding to \(D_i\) is the inverse image of the unit section of \(f_*(R^1 \pi_*)\bar{F}^\alpha\), whence \(D_i^\alpha \simeq (R^1 f_*) \pi_* \bar{F}^\alpha\), which is indeed a constructible sheaf, q.e.d.

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 1.10

It suffices to verify 1.1 in the case where \(S\) is of finite type over \(\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}\), and \(f\) is projective and of relative dimension \(\leqslant 1\).

Proof. Let us first suppose that \(f\) is projective, and proceed by induction on the relative dimension of \(f\), which we may assume finite, possibly after replacing \(S\) by an affine open subset. If \(f\) is of relative dimension \(\leqslant n\), with \(n \geqslant 2\), we can find, locally on \(S\), a finite morphism \(\pi : X \to \mathbb{P}^n_S\), and we reduce, by 1.9 and IX 2.15 (i), to the case where \(f\) is the structural morphism of \(\mathbb{P}^n_S\). Consider the commutative diagram of morphisms
\[\xymatrix{ & \bar{X} \ar[dl] \ar[dr]^{a} \ar[dd]|(0.35){\bar{f}} & \\ \mathbb{P}^n_S \ar[dr]_{f} & & \mathbb{P}^1_S \ar[dl]^{b} \\ & S & }\]

already considered in the proof of XII 8.3, where \(\bar{X}\) is obtained from \(\mathbb{P}^n_S\) by blowing up the closed subscheme \(Y \simeq \mathbb{P}^{n-2}_S\). The relative dimension of \(b\) is \(\leqslant 1\), that of \(a\) is \(\leqslant n-1\), and consequently the theorem is true for \(a\) and \(b\) by the induction hypothesis, hence for \(\bar{f}\) by (1.9). Moreover, the dimension of \(\bar{\pi}\) is \(\leqslant 1\), that of \(f_o : Y \to S\) is \(\leqslant n-1\). It therefore follows from 1.7 that 1.1 is true for \(f\), hence for every projective morphism. Now let \(f\) be an arbitrary proper morphism, and let us proceed by noetherian induction on \(X\): we may assume the theorem true for every closed subscheme distinct from \(X\) and that \(X \neq \emptyset\). Let
\[\xymatrix{ X \ar[dr]_{f} & & \bar{X} \ar[ll]_{\pi} \ar[dl]^{\bar{f}} \\ & S & }\]
a diagram of the type given by Chow's lemma XII 7.1. By applying 1.7 to this diagram, one deduces 1.1 for \(f\), whence the lemma.

1.11. We can now complete the proof of 1.1. If \(F\) is a constructible sheaf of groups, we can find an injection \(F \hookrightarrow G = \prod_i \pi_{i*} C_i\) with \(\pi_i\) finite and \(C_i\) constant and constructible (IX 2.15), and it follows from 1.8 that we may assume \(F\) constant. Similarly, if \(F\) is a constructible sheaf of \(A\)-modules, we can, by applying IX 2.15, find a resolution \(F \to G^\bullet\), \(G^\bullet = \{0 \to G^0 \to G^1 \to G^2 \to \cdots\}\), of \(F\), such that each \(G^\nu\) is of the form \(G^\nu = \prod_i \pi_{i*} C_i\), and one reduces, by the spectral sequence of the resolution \(G^\bullet\),
\[E_2^{p,q} = H^p\big((R^q f_*)G^\bullet\big) \Longrightarrow (R^n f_*)F \;,\]
to the case where \(F\) is constant and constructible, with value \(M\).
Let us recall that \(A\) is a \(\mathbb{Z}/n\)-algebra. Let \(\ell\) be a prime number that divides \(n\). We have the exact sequence
\[0 \to \ell M \to M \to M/\ell M \to 0 \;,\]
and it again suffices to prove 1.1 for \(\ell M\) and \(M/\ell M\).

One then reduces, by an easy induction, to the case where \(A\) is a \(\mathbb{Z}/\ell\)-algebra, \(\ell \in \mathbb{P}\), and where \(M\) is an \(A\)-module of finite type. Then \(M\) is a vector space over \(\mathbb{Z}/\ell\), and consequently the canonical morphism
\[H^q(Y,\mathbb{Z}/\ell) \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}/\ell} M \to H^q(Y,M)\]
is bijective, whatever \(Y\) quasi-compact and quasi-separated may be (indeed, it is trivial if \(M\) is of finite rank, and the two terms commute with inductive limits (VI 1.6)), hence
\[\big[R^q f_*(\mathbb{Z}/\ell)\big] \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}/\ell} M \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } R^q f_*(M) \;.\]

It therefore evidently suffices to prove that \(R^q f_*(\mathbb{Z}/\ell)\) is constructible as a \(\mathbb{Z}/\ell\)-Module, that is, we are reduced to the case \(A = \mathbb{Z}/\ell\), which we assume henceforth.
Note that the case where \(f\) is of relative dimension \(\leqslant 0\) (i.e. where \(f\) is finite) and \(F\) is arbitrary now follows from VIII 5.6 and 1.5.

Let us proceed by noetherian induction on \(S\). By 1.6, we may assume \(S \neq \emptyset\), and allow ourselves to replace \(S\) by any non-empty open subset whatsoever. Moreover, we may assume \(S\) integral, with generic point \(s\). The fibre \(X_s\) is an algebraic scheme of dimension \(\leqslant 1\), and consequently there exists a radicial extension \(K'\) of \(k(s) = K\), such that the normalization \(Y\) of \((X_s \otimes_K K')_{\text{red}}\) is smooth over \(\operatorname{Spec} K'\)(∗). By replacing \(S\) by a non-empty open subset, we may assume that there exists a surjective finite radicial morphism \(S' \to S\) such that \(S'_s\) is \(K\)-isomorphic to \(\operatorname{Spec} K'\), and a surjective finite morphism, a smooth and projective morphism \(\bar{X}' \to S'\) and a surjective finite \(S'\)-morphism \(\pi : \bar{X}' \to X' = X \times_S S'\) which induces \(Y \to X_s \otimes_K K'\) on the fibres at the generic point \(s\) of \(S\) (EGA IV 9.6.1). Now by VIII 1.1 it is harmless to make a radicial extension. We may therefore replace \(S\) by \(S'\) and \(X\) by \(X'\), that is, we may assume that \(f\) fits into a diagram
\[\xymatrix{ X \ar[dr]_{f} & & \bar{X} \ar[ll]_{\pi} \ar[dl]^{\bar{f}} \\ & S & }\]

where \(\pi\) is surjective and finite, and \(\bar{f}\) is smooth. Moreover, by the construction, we may assume that there exists a closed subscheme \(Y\) of \(X\) such that the generic fibre of \(Y\) is finite, and such that \(\pi\) induces an isomorphism over \(X - Y\). By again replacing \(S\) by a non-empty open subset, we reduce to the case where moreover \(f_o : Y \to S\) is a finite morphism.

Since \(F\) is constant, \(\pi^* F\) is likewise constant, and \(F \to \pi_* \pi^* F\) is injective because \(\pi\) is surjective. If \(F\) is a sheaf of groups, it suffices to prove that \((R^1 f_*)(\pi_* \pi^* F) \simeq (R^1 \bar{f}_*)(\pi^* F)\) is constructible (1.8). If \(F\) is a sheaf of \(\mathbb{Z}/\ell\)-modules, we have an exact sequence
\[0 \to F \to \pi_* \pi^* F \to C \to 0 \;,\]

where \(C\) is concentrated on \(Y\), because \(\pi\) induces an isomorphism over \(X - Y\). It follows that \(R^q f_* C = R^q f_{o*} C\) is constructible (zero if \(q > 0\)), and thus it again suffices to prove that \((R^q f_*)(\pi_* \pi^* F) = (R^q \bar{f}_*)(\pi^* F)\) is constructible. Replacing \(f\) by \(\bar{f}\) and \(F\) by \(\pi^* F\), we are reduced to the case where \(F\) is constant and constructible and \(f\) is smooth.

Let us treat the case of a constant sheaf of groups, \(F = G_X\). All the stalks of \((R^1 f_*)G_X\) are finite; indeed, by applying XII 5.2 (ii) we are reduced, in order to prove this, to the case where \(S\) is the spectrum of a separably closed field and where \(X\) is smooth and of dimension \(\leqslant 1\) over \(S\). The result is known in this case (SGA 1 X 2.6). It therefore suffices to prove that the specialization morphisms are injective (IX 2.13 (ii)). For this, we are reduced to the case where \(S\) is strictly local, and by the base change theorem XII 5.1 (ii) we may even replace \(S\) by the spectrum of a strictly local discrete valuation ring. Moreover, we may assume \(X\) connected.

Since \(H^1(X,G)\) classifies the principal Galois coverings of \(X\) with group \(G\), it suffices to verify that if \(X' \to X\) is a connected étale covering then the geometric fibre is likewise connected. This follows easily from the fact that \(f\) is smooth and proper, with connected geometric fibres.

Let us now treat the case \(F = (\mathbb{Z}/\ell)_X\). For the values \(0\) and \(1\) of \(q\) the result is already known ((1.5) and above). By X 4.3 and XII 5.3 bis, there remains only the case \(q = 2\), and moreover, if \(S\) is of characteristic \(\ell\), we have \(R^2 f_*(\mathbb{Z}/\ell) = 0\). By replacing \(S\) by a suitable non-empty open subset, we are therefore reduced to the case where \(\ell\) is invertible on \(S\). Then, by XII 5.2 (ii) and X 4.7, the stalk of \(R^2 f_*(\mathbb{Z}/\ell)\) at a geometric point \(\bar{s}\) over \(s\) is isomorphic to \((\mathbb{Z}/\ell)^{c(s)}\), where \(c(s)\) is the number of irreducible components of dimension \(1\) of the geometric fibre \(X_{\bar{s}}\). Now \(c\) is a constructible function on \(S\) (EGA IV 9.7.9), whence the result (IX 2.13 (iii)).

blocks.title: Remark
blocks.html:
Remark 1.11

The proof of 1.1 is greatly simplified by using the formalism of cohomology with proper supports, which will be developed in XVII as a direct consequence of the base change theorem for a proper morphism XII 5.1. On the other hand, the statement 1.1 generalizes to the case where one is given on \(Y\) an arbitrary sheaf of torsion rings \(\underline{A}\), and one takes on \(X\) a complex \(K^\bullet\) of \(f^*(\underline{A})\)-Modules satisfying a "constructibility" condition which, in the special case 1.1, would be expressed simply by saying that the cohomology sheaves \(\mathscr{H}^i(K^\bullet)\) of \(K^\bullet\) are constructible \(A\)-modules, zero for \(i\) large enough.
2. A variant of dimension.
2.1. Let \(X\) be a scheme. We shall denote
\[d(x) = \dim \overline{\{x\}} \tag{2.1.1}\]
for \(x \in X\), where \(\overline{\{x\}}\) is the closure of \(\{x\}\). If \(F\) is an abelian sheaf on \(X\), we set
\[d(F) = \sup \{d(x) \mid x \in X \text{ and } F_{\bar{x}} \neq 0\} \;. \tag{2.1.2}\]
We shall need a rectified notion in the local case:

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.html:
Definition 2.2

Let \(Y\) be the spectrum of a universally catenary noetherian local ring (EGA IV 5.6.2) and \(f : X \to Y\) a morphism of finite type. Let \(x \in X\) and \(y = f(x)\). We set

\[\delta(x) = \dim \overline{\{y\}} + \operatorname{deg.\,tr.} k(x)/k(y) \;.\]

If \(F\) is an abelian sheaf on \(X\), we set

\[\delta(F) = \sup \{\delta(x) \mid x \in X \text{ and } F_{\bar{x}} \neq 0\} \;.\]

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 2.3
  1. (i) Let \(i : X' \to X\) be an immersion and \(x' \in X'\). Then \(\delta(i(x')) = \delta(x')\).
  2. (ii) Let \(X_o\) be the closed fibre of \(X/Y\). We have \[\delta(x) = \begin{cases} d(x) & \text{if } \overline{\{x\}} \cap X_o \neq \emptyset \\ d(x)+1 & \text{if } \overline{\{x\}} \cap X_o = \emptyset \;; \end{cases}\]
  3. (iii) \(\delta(x) = d(x)\) if \(f\) is proper.

Proof. Assertion (i) is trivial from the definition. Since \(\overline{\{x\}} \cap X_o\) is not empty in the case \(f\) proper, (iii) is a consequence of (ii). For (ii), we can replace \(X\) by \(\overline{\{x\}}\) and \(Y\) by \(\overline{\{y\}}\) (with the induced reduced structure), which is permitted by (i). Let \(x' \in X\) and \(y' = f(x')\). We have the formula (EGA IV 5.6.1.1)
\[\dim \mathcal{O}_{X,x'} = \dim \mathcal{O}_{Y,y'} + \operatorname{deg.\,tr.} k(x)/k(y) - \operatorname{deg.\,tr.} k(x')/k(y') \;.\]
Suppose that \(X_o \neq \emptyset\). Then it is clear that \(\sup_{x'} \{\dim \mathcal{O}_{X,x'}\} = \dim X\) is obtained by taking for \(x'\) a closed point of \(X_o\), whence
\[\dim X = \dim \mathcal{O}_{X,x'} = \dim Y + \operatorname{deg.\,tr.} k(x)/k(y) = \delta(x) \;.\]

If \(X_o = \emptyset\), the supremum is evidently obtained by taking for \(x'\) a closed point in its fibre \(f^{-1}(y')\), such that \(\dim \overline{\{y'\}} = 1\). Such points exist, because the \(y' \in Y\) with \(\dim \overline{\{y'\}} = 1\) form a very dense set (EGA IV 10.1.3, 10.5.9, 1.8.4). We therefore have:
\[\dim X = \dim \mathcal{O}_{X,x'} = \dim Y - 1 + \operatorname{deg.\,tr.} k(x)/k(y) = \delta(x) - 1 \;,\]
whence the result.

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 2.4

Let \(f : X \to Y\) be a morphism of schemes of finite type over the spectrum of a field \(k\). Let \(x \in X\), \(y = f(x)\), and \(y_o\) a specialization of \(y\). Let \(f' : X' \to Y'\) be the strict localization of \(f\) at a geometric point \(\bar{y}_o\) over \(y_o\), and \(x' \in X'\) a point over \(x\). Then we have

\[\delta(x') = d(x) - d(y_o) \;.\]
Proof. We have
\[d(x) = d(y) + \operatorname{deg.\,tr.} k(x)/k(y)\] \[\delta(x') = d(y') + \operatorname{deg.\,tr.} k(x')/k(y') \;,\]
where \(y' = f'(x')\). Moreover
\[\operatorname{deg.\,tr.} k(x)/k(y) = \operatorname{deg.\,tr.} k(x')/k(y') \;,\]
because the extensions \(k(x')/k(x)\) and \(k(y')/k(y)\) are algebraic. It therefore remains to prove that
We may assume \(y\) maximal in \(Y\), hence \(y'\) maximal in \(Y'\), and then

\[\begin{aligned} d(y') &= \dim \mathcal{O}_{Y',\bar{y}_o} \\ &= \dim \mathcal{O}_{Y,y_o} && \text{(EGA IV 6.1.3)} \\ &= \dim Y - d(y_o) && \text{(EGA IV 5.2.3.1)} \\ &= d(y) - d(y_o) \;, \end{aligned}\]
whence the result.

pages.title: 3. Cohomological dimension of affine algebraic schemes.

blocks.html: 3. Cohomological dimension of affine algebraic schemes.

blocks.label: 3.1 (d)
blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 3.1 (d)

Let \(f : X \to Y\) be an affine morphism of schemes of finite type over a field \(k\). Let \(F\) be a torsion sheaf on \(X\) such that \(d(F) \leqslant d\) (cf. 2.1). Then \(d(R^q f_* F) \leqslant d-q\).
In particular, taking \(Y = \operatorname{Spec}(k)\):

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 3.2

Let \(X\) be an affine scheme of finite type over a separably closed field \(k\). Then

\[\operatorname{cd} X \leqslant \dim X \;.\]

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 3.3

Let \(X \subset \mathbb{P}^N_k\) be a projective scheme of dimension \(n\) over a separably closed field \(k\), and let \(Y = H \cap X\) be a "hyperplane section" of \(X\). Then for every torsion sheaf \(F\) on \(X\), the canonical homomorphism

\[H^q_Y(X,F) \longrightarrow H^q(X,F)\]

is bijective for \(q > n+1\), and surjective for \(q = n+1\).

The corollary is trivial from 2.2 and the exact sequence for a closed subset (IV 3.7.1), taking into account that \(X - Y = \mathcal{U}\) is affine of dimension \(\leqslant n\). Let us note that 3.3 is a generalization of one of Lefschetz's theorems on hyperplane sections: indeed, if \(X\) is smooth over \(k\) and \(F\) is locally constant and prime to the characteristic, one can compute the cohomology \(H^q_Y(X,F)\) explicitly using the relative cohomological purity theorem (XVI 3) and the spectral sequence ( ), and one finds that
\[H^q_Y(X, \mathbb{Z}/n) \simeq H^{q-2}(Y, \mu_n^{-1}) \quad \text{for all } q \;;\]
the homomorphism \(H^{q-2}(Y, \mu_n^{-1}) \to H^q(X, \mathbb{Z}/n)\) deduced from 3.3 being none other than the "Gysin homomorphism", which will be studied later(∗).
The theorem 3.1 (d) is equivalent to the following:

blocks.label: 3.4 (d)
blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 3.4 (d)

Let \(Y'\) be a strictly local scheme which is a strict localization of an algebraic scheme over a field. Let \(f' : X' \to Y'\) be an affine morphism of finite type, and \(F'\) a torsion sheaf on \(X'\) such that \(\delta(F') \leqslant d\) (cf. (2.2)). Then \(H^q(X',F') = 0\) for \(q > d\).

Indeed, suppose that 3.4 (d) is true. Let \(f : X \to Y\) be an affine morphism of algebraic schemes over \(k\) and let \(F\) be a torsion sheaf on \(X\) such that \(d(F) \leqslant d\). Let \(y\) be a point of \(Y\) and \(\xi\) a geometric point over \(y\). To prove 3.1 (d), we must prove that the stalk \((R^q f_* F)_\xi\) is zero if \(d(y) > d-q\).
Let \(f' : X' \to Y'\) be the strict localization of \(f\) at the point \(\xi\), that is, let \(Y'\) be the strict localization of \(Y\) at \(\xi\) and let \(X' = X \times_Y Y'\).
Let \(F'\) be the sheaf induced from \(F\) on \(X'\), so that \((R^q f_* F)_\xi = H^q(X',F')\) (VIII 5.2). We have
\[\delta(F') \leqslant d(F) - d(y) \leqslant d - d(y) \tag{2.4}\]
and by applying 3.4 (d), we find \(H^q(X',F') = 0\) if \(q > d - d(y)\), whence the result.

Conversely, suppose that 3.1 (d) is true, and let \(F'\), \(f' : X' \to Y'\) be as in the statement of 3.4 (d). Since cohomology commutes with inductive limits (VII 3.3) and \(F'\) is the inductive limit of its constructible subsheaves (IX 2.9), we may assume \(F'\) constructible. Now \(Y'\) is the strict localization of an algebraic scheme \(Y\) at a geometric point \(\xi\) over a closed point \(y_o\) (X 3.3). Let us write \(Y' = \varprojlim_\alpha Y_\alpha\), where \((Y_\alpha)\) is a filtered projective system of affine schemes étale over \(Y\) (VIII 4.5). By IX 2.7.4, \(F'\) is induced from a constructible torsion sheaf on \(X_\alpha = X \times_Y Y_\alpha\) for \(\alpha\) sufficiently large, and one sees immediately, using 2.4 and EGA IV 9.5.5, that one may moreover assume that \(d(F_\alpha) = \delta(F') \leqslant d\). Replacing \(Y\) by \(Y_\alpha\), we are reduced to the case where \(F'\) is induced by a sheaf \(F\) on \(X\), with \(d(F) \leqslant d\). We then have \(R^q f_* F = 0\) if \(q > d\), by 3.1 (d), hence in particular
\[(R^q f_* F)_\xi = H^q(X',F') = 0 \quad \text{if } q > d,\]
whence 3.4 (d).
As a special case of 3.4 (d), we have

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 3.5

Let \(Y'\) be a strictly local scheme of dimension \(\leqslant d\), the strict localization of an algebraic scheme over a field \(k\). Let \(U \subset Y'\) be an affine open subset. Then \(\operatorname{cd} U \leqslant d\).

blocks.title: Remark
blocks.html:
Remark 3.6

It seems very plausible that 3.4, hence 3.5, remains valid for every noetherian local scheme \(Y'\) (not necessarily a strict localization of an algebraic scheme), at least if \(Y'\) is excellent (EGA IV 7.8). This is what will be proved in (XX 6) when one assumes moreover that \(Y\) is of characteristic zero.

footnotes.html: (∗) Cf. SGA 2 XIV for a systematic study of theorems of Lefschetz type.

blocks.html: 4. Proof of theorem 3.1.
The proof is done by induction on \(d\).

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 4.1

3.1 (0) and 3.1 (1) are true.

Proof. Trivial for \(d = 0\), in which case \(\operatorname{supp} F\) is finite over \(k\), and one applies (VIII 5.5). Let \(F\), \(f : X \to Y\) be as in the statement of 3.1 and suppose that \(d(F) \leqslant 1\). Replacing \(F\) by a constructible subsheaf (IX 2.9 and VII 3.3), we reduce to the case where \(F\) is constructible. Then the support of \(F\) is contained in a closed subscheme of \(X\) of dimension \(\leqslant 1\) (IX 2.3 (ii)), and we may replace \(X\) by this subscheme, that is, we may assume that we have \(\dim X \leqslant 1\). By IX 5.7, the cohomological dimension of an affine algebraic scheme of dimension \(1\) over a separably closed field is \(\leqslant 1\). Moreover, it suffices to treat the case where \(k\) is separably closed: indeed, let \(\bar{f} : \bar{X} \to \bar{Y}\) be the morphism deduced from \(f\) by the base change \(\operatorname{Spec} \bar{k} \to \operatorname{Spec} k\) (\(\bar{k}\) the separable closure of \(k\)). For a geometric point \(\xi\) of \(Y\), the strict localization \(f' : X' \to Y'\) of \(f\) at \(\xi\) is identified with a strict localization of \(\bar{f}\), hence the stalk \((R^q f_* F)_\xi\) with a stalk of \(R^q \bar{f}_* \bar{F}\). Since \(f\) is affine, we therefore find that \(R^q f_* F = 0\) if \(q > 1\). Moreover, it is evident that \(d(f_* F) \leqslant 1\). For the case \(q = 1\), note that the hypothesis that \(X\) be of dimension \(\leqslant 1\) implies that there exists a finite closed subset \(Z\) of \(X\) such that \(f\) is finite over \(Y - Z\). It follows that \(R^1 f_* F\) is zero in \(Y - Z\) (VIII 5.6), whence \(d(R^1 f_* F) \leqslant 1\), which completes the proof of the lemma.
Let \(d \geqslant 2\) and suppose now that 3.1 (d') (or, what amounts to the same, 3.4 (d')) is true for \(d' < d\).

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 4.2

To prove 3.4 (d) in all cases, it suffices to treat the case where \(X' = \mathbb{E}^1_{Y'}\) is the affine space of dimension \(1\) over \(Y'\), and where \(f'\) is the structural morphism.

Proof. Evidently, we may assume \(X' = \mathbb{E}^N_{Y'}\), for suitable \(N\), because we can embed \(X'\) in an \(\mathbb{E}^N_{Y'}\). Suppose \(N > 1\) and the result known for every \(Y'\) and for \(\mathbb{E}^r_{Y'}\), with \(r < N\). Let \(F'\) be a torsion sheaf on \(\mathbb{E}^N_{Y'}\), with \(d(F') \leqslant d\). Consider the diagram
\[\xymatrix{ \mathbb{E}^N_{Y'} \ar[rr]^{g'} \ar[dr]_{f'} & & \mathbb{E}^{N-1}_{Y'} \ar[dl]^{h'} \\ & Y' & }\]

\(g'\) and \(h'\) the canonical projections, so that \(\mathbb{E}^N_{Y'}\) is isomorphic to the affine space of dimension \(1\) over \(\mathbb{E}^{N-1}_{Y'}\). Since evidently each strictly local ring of \(\mathbb{E}^{N-1}_{Y'}\) is also the strict localization of an algebraic scheme, we may apply the induction hypothesis to the stalks of \(R^q g'_* F'\), and we find that
\[\delta(R^q g'_* F') \leqslant d-q \;. \tag{\(*\)}\]
Moreover, 3.4 (d') is true for \(h'\), \(d' \leqslant d\), by the induction hypothesis on \(N\).
Consider the Leray spectral sequence
\[E_2^{p,q} = H^p\big(\mathbb{E}^{N-1}_{Y'}, R^q g'_*(F')\big) \Longrightarrow H^n\big(\mathbb{E}^N_{Y'}, F'\big) \;.\]
We have \(E_2^{p,q} = 0\) if \(p > d-q\), as one finds by applying \((*)\) and 3.4 (d') to the morphism \(h'\). It follows that the abutment is zero if \(n > d\), whence the lemma.
Let us consider the following additional statement, which is a special case of 3.5:

blocks.label: 4.3 (d)
blocks.title: Statement
blocks.html:
Statement 4.3 (d)

Let \(X'\) be strictly local of dimension \(\leqslant d\), the strict localization of an algebraic scheme over a field. Let \(f \in \Gamma(X', \mathcal{O}_{X'})\), and let \(U \subset X'\) be the open set \(U = X' - V(f)\). Then \(\operatorname{cd} U \leqslant d\).

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 4.4

4.3 (d) implies 3.4 (d).
Proof. Consider the diagram
\[\xymatrix{ \mathbb{E}^1_{Y'} \ar[rr]^{i} \ar[dr]_{f'} & & \mathbb{P}^1_{Y'} \ar[dl]^{g'} \\ & Y' & }\]

where \(Y'\) is as in the statement of 2.6 and where \(\mathbb{P}^1_{Y'}\) is the projective space, obtained from \(\mathbb{E}^1\) "by adding the section \(Y'_\infty\) at infinity". Let \(F'\) be a torsion sheaf on \(\mathbb{E}^1\) with \(\delta(\operatorname{supp} F') \leqslant d\). We have the spectral sequence
\[H^p(\mathbb{P}^1, R^q i_* F') \Longrightarrow H^n(\mathbb{E}^1, F') \;.\]

Now the \(R^q i_* F'\), for \(q > 0\), are concentrated on \(Y'_\infty\), which is \(Y'\)-isomorphic to \(Y'\). Since \(Y'\) is strictly local, it follows that \(H^p(Y'_\infty, R^q i_* F') = 0\) if \(p,q > 0\). Moreover, by the base change theorem for a proper morphism (XII 5.1), the cohomology of a torsion sheaf on \(\mathbb{P}^1\) can be computed on the closed fibre, which is a scheme of cohomological dimension \(\leqslant 2\) (X 4.3). We therefore have \(H^p(\mathbb{P}^1, i_* F') = 0\), if \(p > 2\). Since we want to prove \(H^n(\mathbb{E}^1, F') = 0\) for \(n > d\), and since \(d \geqslant 2\), we are reduced to proving that \(H^0(\mathbb{P}^1, R^q i_* F') = 0\) for \(q > d\). This group, also isomorphic to \(H^0(Y'_\infty, R^q i_*(F'))\), is by virtue of (VIII 4.6) isomorphic to the stalk of \(R^q i_* F'\) at the point \(Q\), \(Q\) being the point at infinity of \(\mathbb{P}^1\) in the closed fibre.

It suffices (VII 3.3 and IX 2.9) to treat the case where \(F'\) is constructible. Then, since \(\delta(\operatorname{supp} F') \leqslant d\), there exists a closed subscheme \(X'\) of \(\mathbb{P}^1\) with \(\dim X' \leqslant d\), such that \(X'\) contains the support of \(F'\). Let \(\widetilde{X}'\) be the localization of \(X'\) at the geometric point \(Q\), let \(\widetilde{U} = \widetilde{X}' - \widetilde{X}' \times_{\mathbb{P}^1} Y'_\infty\), and let \(F\) be the sheaf induced by \(F'\) on \(\widetilde{U}\) by the morphism \(\widetilde{U} \to \mathbb{P}^1\). Then the stalk of \(R^q i_* F\) at the point \(Q\) is none other than \(H^q(\widetilde{U},F)\) (VIII 5.2), and one applies 4.3 (d) to the strictly local scheme \(X'\) and to the open set \(\widetilde{U}\).
The lemma below, together with 4.4, will complete the proof.

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 4.5

3.4 (d') for \(d' < d\) implies 4.3 (d') for \(d' \leqslant d\).

Proof. Suppose 3.4 (d') for \(d' < d\). By induction, we may assume that 4.3 (d') is true for \(d' < d\). Let the data \(X'\), \(f\), \(U\) be as in the statement 4.3 (d). Then \(X'\) is the strict localization of an algebraic scheme over a field \(k\) at a closed geometric point \(x_o\). We may take \(X_o\) affine and of dimension \(\leqslant d\), possibly after replacing it by a neighbourhood of \(x_o\). Then \(X'\) is the projective limit of affine and étale schemes \(X_i\) over \(X_o\) (VIII 4.5).

Let \(F\) be a torsion sheaf on \(U\). We must prove that \(H^q(U,F) = 0\) if \(q > d\), and it again suffices to treat the case where \(F\) is constructible. Then the data \(f\), \(F\), \(U\) come from analogous data on one of the \(X_i\) (IX 2.7). We shall have a sheaf \(F_i\) on \(U_i = X_i - V(f_i)\) which "induces" \(F\) on \(U\). Since \(U = \varprojlim U_i\), we have
\[H^q(U,F) = \varinjlim H^q(U_i,F_i) \;.\]
It therefore suffices to prove the following fact: For every \(i\), there exists a commutative diagram
\[\xymatrix{ U \ar[rr] \ar[dr] & & U'' \ar[dl] \\ & U_i & }\]
where \(U \to U_i\) is the given arrow, such that \(\operatorname{cd}(U'') \leqslant d\). Indeed, this will imply that each element of \(H^q(U_i,F_i)\), for \(q > d\), has zero image in \(H^q(U,F)\).

Suppose \(i = 0\), and consider the morphism \(g : X_o \to \mathbb{E}^1_k = Y_o\) given by \(f_o \in \Gamma(X_o, \mathcal{O}_{X_o})\). Let \(Y'\) be the strict localization of \(\mathbb{E}^1_k\) at a geometric point over the origin, so that \(Y'\) is the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring, and let \(X'' = X_o \times_{Y_o} Y'\).

The morphism \(X' \to X_o\) factors through \(X''\) since \(X'\) is strictly local. Moreover, the open set \(U'' = X'' \times_{X_o} U_o\) is none other than the generic fibre of \(X''/Y'\). It is therefore an affine algebraic scheme over the generic point of \(Y'\), and we evidently have \(\dim U'' \leqslant d-1\).

Let us verify that \(\operatorname{cd} U'' \leqslant d\) (which will complete the proof). Let \(K\) be the residue field of \(Y'\) at the generic point. It is a field of cohomological dimension \(1\), that is, we have \(\operatorname{cd}(G) = 1\), \(G\) being the Galois group of the separable closure \(\bar{K}\) of \(K\) (X 2.2). Let \(\bar{U}'' = U'' \times_{\operatorname{Spec} K} (\operatorname{Spec} \bar{K})\). We have \(\operatorname{cd} \bar{U}'' \leqslant d-1\) by the induction hypothesis on \(d\) (this is 2.2 for a scheme of dimension \(\leqslant d\)). The fact that \(\operatorname{cd} U'' \leqslant d\) then follows from the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence (VIII 8.4)
\[H^p(G, H^q(\bar{U}'',\bar{F})) \Longrightarrow H^n(U'',F) \;,\]
whence the lemma 4.5.
